history.summary: The temple crowns the Chaiturgarh (also called Lafagarh) hill fort at about 3,060 ft, an Archaeological Survey of India protected monument on the Korba-Bilaspur road. Inscriptions of the Central Provinces and Berar (Kalchuri Era 933 = 1181-82 CE) trace the Kalchuri lineage of Ratnaraja I to Prithvideva I, and local and popular accounts attribute the fort-temple to Raja Prithvideva I; Wikipedia and lightuptemples place it in this Kalchuri period, while some travel accounts say the Mahishasur Mardini shrine was built in the 10th century by Kalchuri kings - the exact century is uncertain. The sanctum holds a 12-armed Mahishasur Mardini idol; sculptures are in ruins. Local belief holds that Durga slew Mahishasura here. The fort has three entrances (Menaka, Humkara, Simhadwar); a 25-ft Shankar cave lies 3 km from the temple. CSV town correction: the fort is not in Korba town but near Pali village (address Pali 495449), about 70 km from Korba.

name: Chaiturgarh Mahishasur Mardini Temple
town_description: Pali is a village and tehsil on the Korba-Bilaspur road in Korba district, known for the 9th-century Pali Shiva temple and as the base for reaching the Chaiturgarh hill fort nearby.

travel.airport: Bilasa Devi Kevat Airport, Bilaspur, about 90 km away
travel.road: Korba-Bilaspur road; about 70 km from Korba town, 51 km from Katghora; hilltop reached by trek

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri draws a large fair
